text:
**Philip Rubin** is an experimental psychologist and linguist who earned his BA from Brandeis University in 1971 and his PhD in experimental psychology from the University of Connecticut in 1975. His research integrates computational, engineering, linguistic, physiological, and psychological methods to study embodied cognition, particularly focusing on the biological bases of speech and language. Rubin is renowned for his work on articulatory synthesis, speech perception, sinewave synthesis, and signal processing, having developed prominent computational models such as ASY (articulatory synthesis program) and SWS (sinewave synthesis program) in the 1970s at Haskins Laboratories.
Throughout his career, Rubin contributed significantly to speech technology through foundational work on network voice protocols, digitized speech, and digital pattern playback. He co-founded the Auditory-Visual Speech Association (AVISA) and co-created the Talking Heads website. Theoretically, Rubin introduced a dynamical systems/action theory perspective on speech, advocated for a gestural computational model of speech production, and explored perceptual organization through sinewave synthesis. His leadership roles include serving as Director of the Division of Behavioral and Cognitive Sciences at the National Science Foundation and as Assistant Director for Social, Behavioral, and Economic Sciences at the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, where he led initiatives in neuroscience and science policy. Rubin has been active in science advocacy, human research ethics, and remains involved in various scientific organizations, currently serving as the Past President of the Federation of Associations in Behavioral and Brain Sciences (FABBS) and Chair of the Board of Directors at Haskins Laboratories.
